name: 代词使用模式
description: Analyzes pronoun distribution (personal, demonstrative, relative) to detect AI-generated text's distinctive pronoun avoidance patterns.
useCase: Detecting AI text through systematic differences in pronoun usage frequency and variety
mechanism: Categorizes and quantifies pronoun usage across subcategories: first-person (I, we, me), second-person (you, your), third-person (he, she, they), demonstrative (this, that, these), and relative (which, that, who). AI-generated text typically underuses first-person pronouns, overuses impersonal constructions ('it is', 'one can'), and shows less pronominal variety. The method computes pronoun density, category ratios, and positional patterns.
accuracy: Moderate - 70-80% on opinion and narrative text
source: Pennebaker, J. W. (2011) - The Secret Life of Pronouns: What Our Words Say About Us, Bloomsbury Press
algorithm: Pronoun Categorization + Density Analysis + Category Ratio Comparison + Positional Mapping
parameters: Categories: PRP/PRP$/WP/DT, Density: per 100 words, Ratios: 1st/3rd person, self-reference index, Normalization: genre-adjusted
strengths:
• Pronouns carry strong psychological and stylistic signals
• Easy to extract and analyze
• Effective on personal and opinion text
• Backed by extensive psycholinguistic research
limitations:
• Less useful for technical or instructional text
• Cultural and genre differences affect baseline
• AI can be prompted to use specific pronoun patterns
• Needs genre-specific reference distributions

references.title: Pennebaker, J. W. (2011). The Secret Life of Pronouns: What Our Words Say About Us. Bloomsbury Press.
Crothers, E. et al. (2023). Machine-Generated Text: A Comprehensive Survey of Threat Models and Detection Methods. IEEE Access.
Newman, M. L. et al. (2003). Lying Words: Predicting Deception from Linguistic Styles. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin.
